t1kqejni.name: Protests over India election chief
t1kqejni.latestHeadline: India's opposition leader marches with thousands against election chief
t1kqejni.summary: On October 2, thousands of people attended a Mumbai protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party, which asked the election chief to resign. By October 4, police had detained dozens of protesters demanding his resignation over changes to voter rolls, and were accused of sexually harassing journalists at the protest. On October 6, opposition MPs were detained in a protest against the election chief, Gyanesh Kumar, whom opposition leaders alleged had manipulated voter rolls to favour PM Narendra Modi's party. By October 10, a planned protest against the voter roll revision prompted police to order a virtual shutdown of New Delhi and the country's highest court intervened, and on October 12 the opposition leader and thousands of supporters marched towards the Supreme Court over the removal of millions of names from voter lists.

events.headline: US arrests California man for allegedly smuggling $300m worth of computer servers to China
Mapping US chip supply chain: China accounts for far more than it appears, report says

t139atn9.summary: In early October, The Guardian reported that US authorities had arrested a California man, Greg Lui, for allegedly smuggling $300m worth of computer servers to China. He allegedly used false paperwork to move export-controlled gear from the US to third countries and then on to China. In mid-October, the South China Morning Post reported on a Semiconductor Industry Association report on the US chip supply chain. It found that China accounts for about 5 per cent of the equipment and materials directly supplied to the US chip industry by country of manufacture, but holds over 90 per cent of certain rare earths needed for chipmaking.

t1j5n1me.latestHeadline: Houthi official warns US against entering war in Yemen as Saudis weather attacks
t1j5n1me.summary: In early October, Yemen's president announced an all-out war to reclaim land from the Houthis, amid an exchange of strikes between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition. On October 6, Saudi Arabia's aviation authority reported three wounded and severe damage after Houthi strikes on Jazan and Najran airports, and by October 10 fighting between government forces and the Houthis was reported to be intensifying. Around October 11, Trump said he would look at joining Saudi Arabia against the Iran-backed Houthis after a deadly airport strike, and on October 12 Iran was reported to be seeking dialogue on Yemen, warning that a military solution risked complicating the regional situation. By October 13, a Houthi official warned the US of a "painful response" if it entered the war, while Saudi Arabia had reportedly asked Washington for help.

t1rn1bq5.summary: In early October, the euro fell to a 17-month low against the US dollar. Reports linked the drop to concerns about France's ability to bring its public finances in order, and said the currency had lost nearly 7 percent from its peak in late January. At the same time, France's Cac 40 index slid, and the announcement of a snap election in Spain was also reported to be adding to eurozone uncertainty. DW noted that the fall would make inflation worse in the EU, where political worries and concern over French debt were already troubling investors.

t14axxk2.summary: On 5 October, Ukraine's president condemned a Russian strike on a Turkish-owned boat carrying corn in the Black Sea, in which the captain was killed and 11 crew members were rescued. On 6 October, Bulgaria began a search operation after drones hit two ships and the Togo-flagged Alfa Watan sank. On 7 October, Russian authorities said "unmanned boats" attacked a Liberian-flagged tanker off Sochi, sparking a giant fire of oil. By 8 October, France 24 reported that three Turkish-owned cargo ships out of Ukraine had been hit in EU waters by suspected Russian drones, with ten Egyptian and Syrian crew members missing, and on 13 October Bulgaria's prime minister said a drone attack off its coast had sunk a ship and hit two, including the Ukrainian-owned Chelsea 3, which was damaged.

t12s750z.summary: On October 7, IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva said big economies would have to make hard choices as soaring bond yields hit budgets. On October 11, Al Jazeera reported that the US-Israel war on Iran and its inflationary impact, along with high debt, would dominate the IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok. By October 12, US Treasury yields had touched 24-year highs as a global bond sell-off picked up, with the 10-year at 5.36% and the 30-year at 5.73%, the highest for each since 2002. On October 13, yields fell as energy prices pulled back, while some analysts said investors were demanding a higher "term premium" to buy government debt, reflecting worries about debt levels and deficits.

t1qk19hr.summary: In early October, India's central bank raised interest rates for the first time since 2023, with BBC News and CNBC reporting that the move reflected growing inflation concerns. BBC News described it as part of a global shift towards tighter monetary policy as central banks battle inflation fuelled by Middle East conflict. CNBC also reported that HSBC and Goldman Sachs expect the RBI to raise rates again in December. In mid-October, CNBC reported that India's retail inflation rose to 5.54% in September, above estimates, marking the 11th straight month of increase.

By mid-October, Cleveland Fed president Hammack said tighter monetary policy would be needed to bring down inflation.
